slice: Normalize primitive floating aggregate grouping keys
status: optional Rust planner patch; default vendor unchanged

protocol.scope: Normalize only primitive FLOAT/DOUBLE aggregate grouping keys using the existing Rust comparison normalizer. Keep raw aggregate arguments unchanged. Reuse native Aggregate and preserve names/types/qualifiers.
limits: Nested array/struct keys, DISTINCT, DISTINCT aggregate arguments and window partitions are explicit boundary observations, not promised fixes.
SQL cases cover canonical NaN; noncanonical payloads require direct Arrow unit coverage.

supplemental_protocol.why: Initial parent/reference capture revealed constant negative-zero output rules and a PIVOT alias parsing boundary. Add computed constants and alternate pivot placement without changing the original 80 queries.

implementation.rule: Wrap complete FLOAT/DOUBLE grouping keys with the existing Rust SparkComparisonFloat normalizer, preserving the original qualified field name. Traverse grouping-set keys, not operands inside computed keys or aggregate arguments. Ordinary constant expression keys preserve output signs; referenced columns, outer references, scalar subqueries and volatile keys remain eligible for normalization.
implementation.reuse: Native Aggregate and the existing normalizer, including its constant/cast simplification. No new execution node, dependency or Python runtime path.
shared_callers: aggregate projection path with empty grouping

correctness.arrow_unit_coverage: Both float widths and ANSI modes, signed zero, three NaN payloads including a negative NaN, NULL, two input partitions and small batches. Check canonical key sign, grouped row counts, original negative-zero visibility to aggregate arguments, output names/types and native AggregateExec.

iterations.rejected_because: 20 previously passing ordinary constant projections changed negative-zero display to positive zero. Grouping-set constants correctly normalized. Preserve row-independent ordinary keys instead.

setup_failures.failure: Capture wrapper assumed generic IN check records had a status field; this suite validates internally and omits that field. KeyError: status.
setup_failures.fix: Keep process exit validation for both suites; inspect status only in subquery benchmark records. Initial wrapper retained in capture-variant-initial.py.

setup_failures.failure: Compared perf migration counter text with the literal string 0, but perf emitted 0.000000.
setup_failures.fix: Parse numeric counters before comparing with zero; every recorded migration counter is zero.

performance_protocol.purpose: Measure primitive floating grouping normalization using native Aggregate; no change to input data or result count between timed variants.
performance_protocol.inference: Use process medians, paired quartet log ratios and fixed seed 172 / 10000 bootstrap resamples. Retain all controls and observations.
performance_protocol.runtime: 180794d optional runtime plus test-only signed-literal expectation update and floating grouping patch; no type-inference shortcut
performance_protocol.input_limit: Timing inputs are positive finite values; nullable case adds NULL. Outputs equal before/after, keys produce 97/98 groups. SQL and Arrow tests separately cover signed zeros and NaN payloads.

performance_findings: Floating grouping planning adds 6.2-7.7 percent latency, about 0.033-0.046 ms per query in this input. Planning instructions add 6.1-6.9 percent.
Nullable FLOAT grouping execution adds 2.512 percent, interval [2.141,2.886], and 2.211 percent instructions. This local cost remains.

Nonnullable FLOAT execution is 5.340 percent faster in the paired sample while instructions rise 4.647 percent. DOUBLE latency interval spans zero while instructions rise 8.899 percent. These observations do not establish a general execution speedup.
Integer and Decimal execution instruction counts are unchanged to rounding. Their small timing shifts and all same-binary controls are retained; no universal zero-overhead claim.
All 288 processes retained, 100 percent counter coverage, no CPU migrations, unchanged ASLR/governor settings.
Earlier dynamic FLOAT/INT widening and floating USING key normalization costs remain; this comparison does not reevaluate those costs.

parent_production_check.newly_recorded_source: resolver-aggregate.rs is byte-identical to the checked-in parent source
parent_production_check.main_change: Only two test expectation strings; proof in signed-literal-test-results.json
parent_production_check.benchmark_change: Six grouped cases and their expected row counts; identical source for both variants

limitations: 36 new observations still differ: repeated GROUPING_ID bits, DISTINCT, DISTINCT aggregate arguments, nested array/struct keys, window partitioning and PIVOT parser spelling. They remain recorded rather than counted as passes.

The numeric comparator checks values, types and error stages, not full schema metadata or structured error equality. Selected names/types are checked by the Rust test; 116 real Delta queries compare full captured schemas and rows.
Reference SQL uses canonical NaN; direct Arrow tests independently cover alternate NaN payloads.
Nested scalar-subquery execution, duplicate USING-name policy and mixed FULL JOIN output coercion remain outside this slice.
The type-inference shortcut stays deferred and unapplied; its original timing interval is unresolved.
